cpu_small-8src.label: on a laptop
cpu_small-8src.corpus: 8 datasets, at most 500,000 training rows each (3.5M)
cpu_small-8src.changed: The starting point: the normal-payments model alone, no fraud labels used anywhere.

gpu_full-4090.label: on all the data
gpu_full-4090.changed: The same model on seven times the data. It barely moved: the fields it could see, not the number of rows, were the limit.

gpu_full-4090-v4.label: labels, context and the blend
gpu_full-4090-v4.corpus: 9 datasets (AMLworld added), every row (29.2M training rows)
gpu_full-4090-v4.changed: Added decision trees trained on the labelled fraud, the customer's and merchant's recent history as inputs, and a per-bank blend of the two models. The big step: 0.83 to 0.92.

v5-h200-e.label: customer history, entities, extra models
v5-h200-e.hardware: 1x NVIDIA H200 NVL (rented), 64 CPU cores, 188 GB RAM
v5-h200-e.corpus: 11 datasets (BAF, fraudecom added), every row (30M train / 4.3M validation / 8.6M test)
v5-h200-e.changed: The model now reads the customer's previous payments; new facts about the merchant, card, device, e-mail and address around each payment; two more datasets; five extra models. 0.916 to 0.936.

v5-h200-f.label: fresher fraud history
v5-h200-f.hardware: the VAE checkpoint of e; booster side refit on the H200 box (64 CPU cores)
v5-h200-f.changed: Counts fraud confirmed a week ago instead of a month ago, where a bank's labels arrive that fast. The terminal-compromise dataset went from 0.69 to 0.89.

v5-h200-h.label: recent fraud, label timing as a setting
v5-h200-h.hardware: the VAE checkpoint of e; booster side refit on the H200 box (64 CPU cores)
v5-h200-h.changed: Looks at a merchant's fraud over the last 7 and 30 days rather than its whole lifetime, and copes whether or not fresh labels are available. 0.963 average over the nine shared datasets; what shipped until v7.

v6-base-e.label: a pretrained model of payment histories
v6-base-e.hardware: the encoder on a rented node of 8 NVIDIA B200 GPUs (60,000 steps, four and a half hours); the VAE checkpoint of e; booster side refit on one of them
v6-base-e.corpus: the encoder: 16 datasets (five more AMLworld variants), 328M training rows, no labels; the booster as e
v6-base-e.changed: A large model that read 328 million payments with no fraud labels and learnt what a customer's next payment looks like. What it makes of a customer's history goes to the decision trees. A big gain for the bank with long card histories (86% to 94% of its fraud caught), a small loss for three others.

v7-f.label: the history model where it helps
v7-f.hardware: the encoder of v6, unchanged; the VAE checkpoint of e; booster side refit on a rented box with 2x NVIDIA H200 NVL
v7-f.changed: Uses the history model only for the two banks where it earned its place, adds a small model trained on fraud labels on top of it, and lets the verdict rest on the models that learnt fraud. More fraud caught at the same false-alarm rate on average, 86% to 95% for the bank with long card histories, and no bank worse; what ships.
